product_or_service: Ledgerly Payroll (SaaS payroll and tax-filing service)
summary: Ledgerly Payroll will replace in-house payroll spreadsheets for 180 employees. It will receive names, addresses, SSNs, salaries and bank account numbers through a one-way HR sync, and 6 staff will sign in through SSO. The vendor is provisionally Tier 2 (High) because of employee PII and financial data, an HR-system integration and an important process with a one-cycle manual workaround. Open intake questions could move it to Tier 1: funding-debit or tax-agent authority, whether the workaround survives migration, HR connector credentials and fields, and record volume. The SOC 2 Type II report (July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026) is an excerpt with selected tests only. It has an unqualified opinion, covers Ledgerly Payroll and shows no exceptions for workforce MFA, access reviews, pen testing, logging, incident response, backups and change management. The DPA excerpt includes subprocessor notice, 72-hour breach notice, deletion and no ML training, but it is unsigned, so the contract-based domains (2, 8, 10, 12) are partially met. No claim was contradicted by evidence. The 1-hour RPO claim is unsupported, since only daily backups and restore tests are evidenced. Three medium findings remain: encryption of SSNs and bank data rests on claims only, oversight of the carved-out AWS and Evergreen Bank is not evidenced, and customer-side authentication is not evidenced (portal MFA, bank-detail change verification, SSO enforcement), along with vendor-staff deprovisioning. Several low evidence gaps remain. The recommendation is approve with conditions, subject to the requesting team's intake answers.

data_types: Bank account numbers for direct deposit
Former-employee records retained about 4 years after termination (per PRV-2)
inherent_risk.access_level: One-way sync from our HR system to Ledgerly (new hires and terminations), so Ledgerly does not write back to our systems. SAML SSO for 6 Finance and People Operations users. Still unconfirmed: whether Ledgerly will debit our operating account, hold company bank details and the EIN, or act as our tax reporting agent; how the HR connector is authenticated and with what permissions; and whether the employee self-service portal will be enabled for all 180 employees.
inherent_risk.criticality: Important: payroll must run on schedule, but the intake says a manual off-cycle run is possible for one cycle. Whether this workaround survives retirement of the in-house spreadsheets is unconfirmed.
inherent_risk.rationale: Tiered from the intake note before reviewing vendor evidence, taking the highest tier any factor points to. Data: employee PII and financial records (SSNs, salaries, bank accounts) point to Tier 2. No payment card data, credentials or PHI are declared. The 'not a large volume' reasoning is provisional until record counts, including migrated history and former employees, are known. Access: an integration with a core system (HR) points to Tier 2. Criticality: an important process with a workaround points to Tier 2. The tier is provisional. Re-tier to Tier 1 and re-apply the outcome guide if the requesting team confirms any of the following: Ledgerly will debit company accounts or file and pay taxes as our agent (comparable to privileged access to a financial system); the manual workaround is not credible after migration; health-related HR fields reach the vendor; or Ledgerly stores a write-capable HR API credential.

soc2.opinion: Unqualified. Section 1: the controls 'were suitably designed and operated effectively throughout the period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.'
soc2.scope_notes: Section 3 places Ledgerly Payroll in scope: payroll processing, tax calculation and filing, direct deposit, employee self-service portal and HR system integrations. Trust Services Criteria covered are Security, Availability and Confidentiality; Privacy and Processing Integrity are not covered. The excerpt is abridged and shows only selected Section 4 tests, so exclusions and other tested controls are not visible; the full report has been requested. Control AC-02 covers Ledgerly workforce and administrative access, not customer end-user portal accounts. The period ended about 4.7 months before the review date, inside the 6-month window. It crosses 6 months on 2026-12-31.
subservice_orgs: Amazon Web Services (us-east-1, us-east-2): infrastructure hosting, carved out
Evergreen Bank, N.A.: ACH origination for direct deposit, carved out

We must review payroll registers before approving each payroll run

controls.evidence: No security policy set, policy approval dates or governance documentation was provided. The questionnaire header names P. Okafor as Security Lead, which is a claim only.

DPA Section 4 commits Ledgerly to a current subprocessor list, 30 days' notice of additions and a customer right to object, but the DPA is unsigned and still under review, so this is not yet a signed contract term. SOC 2 Section 3 lists AWS and Evergreen Bank as carved-out subservice organizations, which matches questionnaire SUB-1. No evidence shows Ledgerly monitors these organizations or flows down security terms to them. The subprocessor web page was not reviewed.

SOC 2 AC-02 (CC6.1): MFA enforced for Ledgerly workforce and administrative access, 25 accounts sampled, no exceptions. AC-05 (CC6.2): quarterly access reviews, four inspected, no exceptions. The following are not evidenced: customer SAML SSO and SCIM (IAM-2, claim only); timely deprovisioning of Ledgerly staff and least privilege (no test in the excerpt); and authentication of end-user employee self-service portal accounts, including MFA and verification of direct-deposit changes. The portal is in SOC 2 scope, but AC-02 does not cover customer end users. CUEC 1 makes us responsible for deprovisioning our own users.

Questionnaire DAT-1 claims TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest with AWS KMS and field-level encryption of bank account numbers. No SOC 2 encryption test appears in the excerpt. DPA Section 7 refers to Annex 2 technical measures, which was not provided.
SOC 2 LM-03 (CC7.2): 'Security events are centrally logged and alerts triaged 24x7'; SIEM configuration and an alert sample were inspected, no exceptions. Log retention period not stated.

SOC 2 VM-01 (CC7.1): independent pen test report dated May 6, 2026 and remediation tickets inspected, no exceptions. The test is within 12 months of the review date. Patch SLAs (VUL-2: critical 7 days, high 30 days, medium 90 days) and vulnerability scanning are claims only. The pen test executive summary said to be attached to the questionnaire was not provided.
SOC 2 CH-01 (CC8.1): production changes reviewed and approved, 40 changes sampled, no exceptions. No evidence on code review, security testing in CI or dependency management.

SOC 2 IR-01 (CC7.4): IR plan maintained and tested annually (plan and tabletop inspected), no exceptions. DPA Section 9 provides notice 'without undue delay, and in any event within 72 hours' after confirming an incident, which matches INC-1. However, the DPA is unsigned and still under review (intake), so the notification term is not yet a signed contract term. The 72-hour clock starts at confirmation, with no bound on the time from detection to confirmation. No named incident contact is shown.

SOC 2 BC-02 (A1.2): daily backups and quarterly restore tests inspected, no exceptions. The BCP-1 claim of 'RTO 8 hours, RPO 1 hour; tested quarterly' is unsupported. Daily backups alone would not deliver a 1-hour RPO, and no replication or point-in-time recovery mechanism is evidenced. A restore test is not an RTO/RPO test. No BC/DR plan or DR exercise evidence was provided.

DPA Section 11: export available for 60 days after termination, deletion within 30 days after any legally required retention period, written confirmation on request. The DPA is unsigned and still under review, so this is not yet a signed contract term. The US-only data location claim (DAT-2) is consistent with the AWS us-east-1/us-east-2 regions in SOC 2 Section 3, but the DPA excerpt contains no data-location commitment. The claim that support staff are US-based is unsupported. PRV-2 states payroll records are retained for about 4 years after termination. The Privacy TSC is not in SOC 2 scope.
No evidence or claims about background checks, security awareness training or confidentiality agreements appear in any document provided.

Questionnaire PRV-1 claims customer data is not used for model training (claim). DPA Section 12: 'Ledgerly will not use Customer Personal Data to train or improve machine learning models.' The DPA is unsigned and still under review, so this is not yet a signed contract term. The clause also covers Customer Personal Data only, which is narrower than the questionnaire's 'customer data'.

findings.title: Encryption of SSNs and bank account data not independently evidenced
findings.description: Encryption in transit, encryption at rest and field-level encryption of bank account numbers are supported only by questionnaire answers. The vendor will hold SSNs and bank account numbers for all employees, so this claim is important for a Tier 2 vendor. Confidentiality is in SOC 2 scope, so the full report may contain relevant tests. Because the full report and DPA Annex 2 are low-cost to obtain, resolving this before employee data is loaded is advisable.
findings.evidence: questionnaire.md DAT-1: 'TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest with AWS KMS; bank account numbers additionally encrypted at the field level.' The SOC 2 excerpt ('Tests of Controls and Results (selected)') contains no encryption test. DPA Section 7 refers to 'Annex 2', which was not provided.
findings.recommendation: Request DPA Annex 2 and the full SOC 2 report, including the Section 4 tests covering encryption in transit and at rest and key management (CC6.1/CC6.7). Also request evidence of field-level encryption of bank account numbers and of how SSNs are protected. Close the finding if tested without exception. Preferably resolve before data is loaded.

findings.recommendation: Request evidence of Ledgerly's annual review of the AWS and Evergreen Bank assurance reports (SOC report reviews and CUEC mapping), or the full SOC 2 test of vendor management (CC9.2). Also request confirmation that security and breach-notification terms flow down to Evergreen Bank.

findings.recommendation: Request the information security policy index with approval and last-review dates, and confirmation of the accountable security executive. Close against the full SOC 2 report if covered there. Track at next review.

findings.evidence: No relevant content appears in questionnaire.md, soc2-type2-excerpt.md (selected tests only) or dpa-excerpt.md.
findings.recommendation: Request the full SOC 2 Section 4 results for personnel controls (CC1.4/CC2.2), or equivalent evidence of background checks, annual training completion and signed confidentiality agreements. Track at next review.

findings.description: Change approval is tested with no exceptions, which partially compensates. Code review, security testing in CI and dependency management are not evidenced.
findings.evidence: soc2-type2-excerpt.md CH-01 (CC8.1): 'Production changes reviewed and approved', 40 changes sampled, no exceptions. No other SDLC evidence was provided.
findings.recommendation: Request evidence of mandatory code review, SAST and dependency scanning in CI, and the dependency vulnerability remediation process. Track at next review.

findings.title: 1-hour RPO and RTO claims unsupported; only daily backups and restore tests evidenced
findings.description: Daily backups and quarterly restore tests are evidenced. The questionnaire's '1 hour' RPO 'tested quarterly' is in tension with this evidence. Daily backups alone cannot deliver a 1-hour RPO, and no replication or point-in-time recovery mechanism is evidenced. A restore test is also not a test of achieved RTO/RPO. The claim is classified as unsupported rather than contradicted, because another recovery mechanism may exist. If the vendor confirms that daily backups are the only mechanism, this becomes a contradiction and a high finding. Payroll timing and tax deadlines are important to the business, and no BC/DR plan or exercise was provided.
findings.evidence: soc2-type2-excerpt.md BC-02 (A1.2): 'Daily backups; quarterly restore tests', no exceptions. questionnaire.md BCP-1: 'RTO 8 hours, RPO 1 hour; tested quarterly' (claim).
findings.recommendation: Ask the vendor to identify the mechanism supporting the 1-hour RPO and to provide the most recent DR exercise showing achieved RTO and RPO. Also request the BC plan's provisions for meeting payroll and tax-filing deadlines during an outage. Re-rate to high and record a contradiction if daily backups are the only mechanism.

findings.title: US data location and US-based support not contractually committed
findings.description: US-only storage and processing is consistent with the SOC 2 AWS regions, but the DPA excerpt contains no data-location commitment. US-based support staff is a claim only. Data may also be retained for about 4 years after termination, and it is unclear whether bank account numbers fall within that retention.
findings.evidence: questionnaire.md DAT-2: 'United States only (AWS us-east-1 and us-east-2). Support staff are US-based.' soc2-type2-excerpt.md Section 3 lists AWS us-east-1/us-east-2. dpa-excerpt.md has no location clause. questionnaire.md PRV-2 gives retention of 'generally 4 years under IRS rules'.
findings.recommendation: Seek a DPA clause restricting storage, processing and support access to the United States. Ask the vendor to confirm which data elements are kept during the legal retention period, and that data not required by law (for example bank account numbers) is deleted at the standard 30-day point.

findings.title: No-ML-training commitment limited to personal data and not yet signed
findings.description: The DPA's ML prohibition covers 'Customer Personal Data' only, while the questionnaire states more broadly that 'customer data' is not used for model training. Non-personal customer data, such as aggregate payroll or company financial data, is not covered. The DPA is also not yet executed.
findings.evidence: dpa-excerpt.md Section 12: 'will not use Customer Personal Data to train or improve machine learning models.' questionnaire.md PRV-1: 'Customer data is not used for model training.' intake.md: 'Data Processing Addendum under review'.
findings.recommendation: Request that DPA Section 12 (or the order form) be extended to all Customer Data, including aggregated or de-identified derivatives, or that the vendor confirm in writing how non-personal data is used. Execute the DPA before signature.

findings.title: Customer-side authentication, portal account protection and vendor-staff deprovisioning not evidenced
findings.description: The SOC 2 evidence covers only Ledgerly's own workforce MFA and quarterly access reviews. Several controls that protect our accounts are not evidenced: customer SAML SSO/SCIM and enforcement of our IdP's MFA (claim only); MFA for employee self-service portal accounts; out-of-band verification and notification of direct-deposit bank-detail changes (payroll-diversion risk); and timely deprovisioning and least privilege for Ledgerly staff. Whether the portal will be enabled for all 180 employees is an open intake question.
findings.evidence: soc2-type2-excerpt.md AC-02 (CC6.1): 'MFA enforced for all workforce and administrative access'. AC-05 (CC6.2): quarterly access reviews. Section 3 scope includes 'employee self-service portal'. questionnaire.md IAM-2: 'Yes, SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning' (claim). No document addresses end-user MFA or verification of bank-detail changes.
findings.recommendation: Request evidence of end-user portal MFA and of out-of-band verification and dual notification of bank-detail changes, plus the full SOC 2 tests of joiner/mover/leaver and least-privilege controls (CC6.2/CC6.3) and confirmation that customer SAML SSO enforces our IdP's MFA. Re-rate to high if the portal is enabled for employees and these controls cannot be evidenced. Do not enable employee portal self-service changes to bank details until resolved.

outcome_rationale: On the provisional Tier 2 rating, there are no critical or high findings and no claims contradicted by evidence. The SOC 2 Type II has an unqualified opinion, covers the purchased product, ended within 6 months of the review date and shows no exceptions in the selected key controls. Three medium findings (F-01 encryption, F-02 subservice oversight, F-09 customer-side authentication) and several low findings remain. The contract terms relied on for domains 2, 8, 10 and 12 sit in a DPA that is not yet executed. Under the outcome guide, several mediums support approval with conditions. This outcome depends on the requesting team's answers on funding-debit and tax-agent authority, the manual workaround, HR connector credentials and fields, and record volume. If any answer moves the vendor to Tier 1, or F-06 or F-09 is raised to high, re-apply the outcome guide. Under that guide, high findings in a Tier 1 vendor without a committed fix lead to escalation. The final decision rests with the human risk owner.
conditions: Before the outcome is finalized (internal): the requesting team answers the open intake questions on funding-debit and tax-agent authority, employee portal enablement and sign-in, the post-migration manual payroll workaround and tax-deadline plan, HR connector authentication and fields, and record volume. If any answer meets a Tier 1 factor, re-tier and re-apply the outcome guide.

Before signature: execute the DPA with Sections 4 (subprocessor notice), 7 (security measures, with Annex 2 attached), 9 (72-hour incident notification, preferably bounded from discovery), 11 (return and deletion) and 12 (no ML training), each at least as protective as the reviewed excerpt.

Within 90 days (F-01), preferably before employee data is loaded: vendor provides the full SOC 2 report and Annex 2, or equivalent evidence, of encryption in transit and at rest, key management, and field-level protection of bank account numbers and SSNs.
Within 90 days (F-02): vendor provides evidence of its oversight of AWS and Evergreen Bank, including assurance report reviews and flow-down of security and breach terms.

Within 90 days (F-09), and before enabling employee self-service bank-detail changes: vendor evidences end-user portal MFA, out-of-band verification and notification of bank-detail changes, enforcement of our IdP's MFA through SAML SSO, and Ledgerly staff deprovisioning and least-privilege controls.

Before go-live (internal): assign named owners for the three CUECs (deprovisioning our users, pre-approval review of payroll registers, accuracy of the HR data sync), and require access only through our SSO with MFA for the 6 admin users.

At next review (12 months): track low findings F-03 to F-08, re-rating F-06 to high if daily backups prove to be the only recovery mechanism. Obtain the next SOC 2 Type II report (period after June 30, 2026), or a bridge letter if the new report is not yet issued.

challenge_log.challenge: The intake does not declare company bank details, the EIN, debit authority over our operating account, or tax-agent authority. A payroll and tax-filing service with ACH direct deposit usually needs all of these, which could push the vendor to Tier 1.
challenge_log.response: Requesting team to answer. The documents support the concern but do not settle it. SOC 2 Section 3 scope covers 'payroll processing, tax calculation and filing, direct deposit'. Evergreen Bank performs 'ACH origination for direct deposit'. The intake lists only employee data and a 'one-way sync from our HR system'. The tier must be set from the intake, so it stays Tier 2 provisionally. If the team confirms that Ledgerly will debit our accounts or file and pay taxes as our agent, re-tier against the Access factor before the outcome is finalized. Authority to move company funds is comparable to privileged access to a financial system. Then re-apply the outcome guide: high findings in a Tier 1 vendor without a committed fix lead to escalation. If confirmed, also add vendor questions on funding-debit controls and protection of our company bank credentials.

challenge_log.challenge: The employee self-service portal is in SOC 2 scope, but the intake counts only 6 SSO users. End-user MFA and verification of direct-deposit bank changes are not evidenced, which creates a payroll-diversion risk.
challenge_log.response: Requesting team to answer whether the portal will be enabled for 180 employees, and how they will sign in. The vendor must answer the control questions. The challenge's facts check out. SOC 2 Section 3 lists an 'employee self-service portal' in scope. AC-02 covers 'workforce and administrative access', meaning Ledgerly staff, not customer end users. No document addresses end-user MFA or verification of bank-detail changes. Whatever the team answers, add a vendor follow-up question now: is MFA enforced for portal accounts, and are bank-account changes verified out of band and notified to both the employee and the customer admin? If the portal is enabled and the vendor cannot evidence these controls, add a domain 3 finding rated high for a Tier 2 vendor.

challenge_log.challenge: The 'manual off-cycle run' workaround may not be credible once the spreadsheets are retired. If so, criticality points to Tier 1.
challenge_log.response: Requesting team to answer. The intake states a workaround exists ('a manual off-cycle run is possible for one cycle'). Its stated purpose is also to 'replace our in-house payroll spreadsheets', so whether the workaround survives migration cannot be settled from the documents. The Tier 2 criticality rating stands only if the team confirms an owned and tested offline procedure, plus a plan for tax deadlines. If the workaround is not credible, criticality meets the Tier 1 definition ('outage stops a critical business process'). In that case, re-tier and re-apply the outcome guide. On the vendor side, the existing follow-up question on the DR exercise and business-continuity provisions for payroll and tax deadlines (F-06) remains.

challenge_log.challenge: The intake does not say how the HR sync is authenticated, which fields it exposes, or whether history will be migrated. All three affect data minimization, record volume and possible health-related fields.
challenge_log.response: Requesting team to answer. The intake gives only 'one-way sync from our HR system (new hires and terminations)'. Questionnaire PRV-2 confirms retention for about 4 years after termination, so Ledgerly will hold former-employee records beyond the 180 current staff. The draft's tier reasoning ('180 employee records is not a large volume') should be revisited once actual record counts are known. The answer would change the tier if health-related fields (for example leave reasons) reach the vendor, since regulated health data points to Tier 1. The same applies if Ledgerly stores a write-capable HR API credential, which matters for the 'credentials or keys' factor. No review change is needed until the team answers.

challenge_log.challenge: BCP-1 claims a 1-hour RPO 'tested quarterly', but the only tested control is daily backups with quarterly restore tests. The challenge argues this is a contradiction and should be a high finding.
challenge_log.response: Vendor to answer. The evidence shows a tension but not a contradiction. SOC 2 BC-02 evidences 'Daily backups; quarterly restore tests'. It does not state that daily backups are the only recovery mechanism. Continuous replication or point-in-time recovery could coexist and would support a 1-hour RPO. Under questionnaire-gap-check, the claim is therefore 'unsupported', not 'contradicted', and is not a high-severity contradiction finding. The challenge is right that a restore test is not an RTO/RPO test. Revise F-06 to describe this tension. Add the vendor question: what mechanism supports the 1-hour RPO, and please provide the latest test showing achieved RTO and RPO. If the vendor confirms daily backups are the only mechanism, record a contradiction between BCP-1 and BC-02 and raise it to a high finding.

challenge_log.challenge: Domains 8 and 12 are marked 'met' on DPA terms, but the DPA is unsigned and still under review. The 72-hour notice clock also starts only 'after confirming' an incident.
challenge_log.response: Change domain 8 to partially_met. The IR plan and its testing are evidenced by SOC 2 IR-01 (CC7.4, no exceptions). The notification term in DPA Section 9 is not yet a signed contract term, and no named contact is shown. Change domain 12 to partially_met. It rests on questionnaire PRV-1, which is a claim, plus DPA Section 12, which is unexecuted (intake: 'Data Processing Addendum under review'). SKILL.md step 3 treats only a 'signed contract term' as evidence. Add vendor questions asking Ledgerly to bound the time from detection to confirmation, or to commit to notice within 72 hours of discovery. Keep the pre-signature DPA condition. The outcome is unchanged. Domains 2 and 10 also rely on DPA terms and are already partially_met; add the same note to their evidence.

challenge_log.challenge: Domain 3 is marked 'met', but customer SSO/SCIM, Ledgerly staff deprovisioning and end-user portal authentication are not evidenced.
challenge_log.response: Change domain 3 to partially_met. The control catalog's good evidence for this domain includes 'SSO, MFA enforced for all users and especially admins, least privilege, timely deprovisioning, periodic access reviews'. The SOC 2 excerpt evidences only workforce MFA (AC-02) and quarterly access reviews (AC-05). The draft itself calls IAM-2 SAML/SCIM 'a claim only'. No test covers deprovisioning of Ledgerly staff or least privilege, and end-user portal authentication is open (see C2). Add vendor follow-up questions asking for the SOC 2 tests of joiner/mover/leaver and least-privilege controls (CC6.2/CC6.3) and evidence that customer SAML SSO enforces our IdP's MFA.

challenge_log.challenge: Findings F-01 to F-05 may only reflect missing pages of an abridged SOC 2 report. The challenge proposes closing or re-rating them against the full report.
challenge_log.response: Vendor to answer by supplying the full SOC 2 Type II report. The findings cannot be removed now. The only report provided is labelled 'Excerpted and abridged' with 'Tests of Controls and Results (selected)'. Assuming the full report 'normally' tests CC1.4, CC6.7 or CC9.2 would treat absence of evidence as a pass and invent evidence, which the guardrails prohibit. F-01 to F-05 stay open at their current rubric severities. Add a vendor request for the complete report, including Section 4. When it arrives, close any finding whose control is tested without exception and re-rate the rest. Because the full report and DPA Annex 2 are low-cost to obtain, note for the risk owner that resolving F-01 (encryption of SSNs and bank data) before data is loaded is advisable. It does not have to wait for the 90-day due date.

challenge_log.challenge: The challenge argues a bridge letter should be requested now to cover July 1, 2026 onward, rather than deferred to the 12-month review.
challenge_log.response: The soc2-report-reader rule calls for a bridge letter only 'if the period ended more than 6 months before the review date'. The period ended 2026-06-30, and the review date is 2026-11-20, about 4.7 months later. The draft's 'bridge_letter_needed: false' is therefore correct, and no finding is warranted. The low-severity rubric example ('missing bridge letter') applies only once the rule is triggered. One note to add to Limitations: the report crosses the 6-month mark on 2026-12-31. If contract signature or go-live falls after that date, a bridge letter becomes due, and the next SOC 2 issue date should be confirmed then.
